findings.where: Nav bar (the gummed binding): the aqueduct mark and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark, at both widths
findings.fault: The logo has been recoloured. Its arches and wordmark are drawn in pale canary on the brown binding, not the logo blue #0070C0 and grey #404040. No palette token picks up either logo colour, and the palette doesn't mark them as logo-only, so the identity tile leaves out the client's only fixed brand colours. This is a reversed, single-colour logo that the client doesn't hold and hasn't approved.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo stays as it is under the brand sheet. A visitor who knows his current site or business card sees a mark in different colours, and the next round inherits a palette with no rule for where the real blue-and-grey logo can sit.

findings.where: The page ground on every view: the ruled lines and the double margin line down the left, at both widths, set against the Palette section's 'Feint #93B3D3, rules' and 'Margin red #B8322B, margin' swatches and the blue rules in the Texture specimen
findings.fault: The page doesn't use its own palette. Its rules are a dull olive-grey, not the pale feint blue in the swatch and the texture sample, and its margin line is a dark olive-brown double line, not margin red. The two colours that make a canary pad read as a legal pad (blue rules, red margin) appear only in the specimens. The page itself looks like a yellow sheet ruled in brown.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who chose the legal pad because of his legal background and would not recognise one here. The designer of the layout round would also object, because the tile's swatches and its rendered ground disagree about which colours to build with.

findings.where: The ruled ground behind text: the motion sketch's timeline table (desktop-03 and phone-03, rows at 24 px leading across 32 px rules), the hero headline's lines, and the 'Libre Caslon Text' specimen heading
findings.fault: The rules are dark enough to cut through any text that isn't set on the 32 px ruling. They strike through the table cells and run behind the large headings, so those blocks look crossed out and noisy instead of written on the pad.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader skimming an article or table, who has to read past lines that look like strikethrough. Angélique would object too: any post or PDF list she adds that doesn't keep the exact line spacing will look the same.

findings.where: Palette section, 'Ballpoint #1B2A6B' and 'Light hand #34407A'; in use as the article headline against the handwritten pull quote, and the type against the hatching in the aqueduct sketch
findings.fault: Ballpoint and Light hand are two navy inks so close that they read as the same blue at every size on the page. The 'Light hand' role (asides, hatching) can't be seen, so it looks like a near-miss mistake rather than a second ink.
findings.who_objects: Whoever applies the tokens next (the layout round, Angélique). They get two names for one visible colour and can't tell which one a part uses or why.

findings.where: Edges of the bordered parts: the palette swatches (olive-grey outline), the Texture specimen and the easing-curve frame (cool grey), the motion sketch panel (navy), and the article's PDF row dividers (navy)
findings.fault: There are four edge colours with no stated roles, and two of them are greys that aren't in the palette. Parts of the same kind (specimen frames on the same pad) get different border colours.
findings.who_objects: The designer of the layout round, who needs one decorative-edge colour to carry forward and instead finds four, two of them from outside the stated palette.
